## Purpose and scope

This roadmap owns the metaplectic side of automorphic forms: the Heisenberg group of a symplectic space and its Schrödinger models, the Stone–von Neumann theorem, the metaplectic double cover with its Weil representation, the Weil index, local theta correspondences for reductive dual pairs, the adelic metaplectic group with its rational splitting and global Weil representation, theta kernels and genuine automorphic forms on the cover, the Siegel–Weil and Rallis formulas with the theta integrals other roadmaps consume, the Jacobi group and Jacobi forms, the half-integral-weight theory behind the Shimura correspondence, and the genus-two Bump–Friedberg–Hoffstein Eisenstein series whose polar formula RankZeroOneBSD BSD.2 uses for quadratic-twist nonvanishing. A central cover is not a reductive group, so the cocycle, the splittings, the topology and the genuine central character are part of every construction. The roadmap begins over local fields of characteristic zero, with a nontrivial continuous additive character and self-dual Haar measures; local fields of positive characteristic, global function fields and finite fields lie outside it (see "What is not here").

- **MP.0, Heisenberg groups and Schrödinger models.** The Heisenberg group as Tau Ceti's factor-set extension of a bilinear form, in characteristic two as well, with its inverse, commutator and center; the half-alternating convention B = ½ω when 2 is invertible; the action of the isometry group and polarized coordinates; the central character extended trivially along the canonical section; the topology, product Haar measure, Schrödinger model on Schwartz–Bruhat functions, its induced form, the Hilbert model on L² and its smooth vectors.
- **MP.1, Stone–von Neumann and the metaplectic extension.** The smooth and unitary Stone–von Neumann theorems; the normalizer extension of Sp(W) by the circle, with its scalar ambiguity; Rao's normalized μ₂-valued factor set; the metaplectic double cover Mp(W) = ker λ₂ and the genuine Weil representation, on which the central −1 acts by −1.
- **MP.2, Weil index and explicit operator formulas.** The Weil index γ_ψ(q) as a Fourier scalar of an oscillatory distribution, its Hilbert-symbol identities including the dyadic case, the Leray invariant and Leray cocycle, the Weil operators on Levi, unipotent and Fourier generators and their relations, change of character and duality, and the quadratic and Hermitian uncertainty principles with the Hermitian operator normalizations of the unitary arithmetic papers.
- **MP.3, dual pairs and local theta modules.** Orthogonal–symplectic and unitary dual pairs with their splittings; big and small theta; finite length and Howe duality in their sourced ranges; see-saws, persistence, first occurrence, Kudla's Jacquet filtration, the doubling filtration and the conservation relations; unitary dichotomy, unramified parameters and Hecke compatibility; Ichino–Prasanna's quaternionic similitude splittings; and the classical theta lifts that the exceptional correspondences of Gan–Savin use as inputs.
- **MP.4, the adelic cover and the global Weil representation.** Unramified compact splittings, the adelic cover as a restricted product modulo the product-one central subgroup, Weil's product formula, the canonical rational splitting, the adelic and finite Weil representations, compatibility with every choice, and Lafforgue's conditional function-field programme recorded as a programme.
- **MP.5, theta kernels, convergence and automorphic spaces.** The theta kernel, its smoothness and moderate growth, genuine automorphic forms with their constant terms and Whittaker coefficients, genuine Eisenstein families, the global theta lift, Weil's convergence criterion and the regularized theta integral; Yuan–Zhang's extended Schwartz spaces and unit-quotiented theta series; and the ideal-class theta series of an imaginary quadratic field with its modularity and transformation law.
- **MP.6, local–global comparison and reusable theta integrals.** Measure conventions, Siegel–Weil sections, the anisotropic Siegel–Weil formula and the regularized first- and second-term identities of Gan–Qiu–Takeda, coherent and incoherent sections, the doubling method of the theta pairing and the Rallis inner product formula, the global see-saw, the norm-form theta integrals and toric pairing exported to Gross–Zagier, and the general Jacobi group, Jacobi spaces, Fourier–Jacobi extraction and theta decomposition.
- **MP.7, half-integral weight, metaplectic Fourier coefficients and twists.** The theta multiplier, weight-one-half Maass forms and Eisenstein series, the Kohnen plus space, half-weight Kloosterman sums, resolvent and Poincaré series, the Kohnen–Salié identity and the three cycle-integral cases of Duke–Imamoḡlu–Tóth, the Shimura correspondence with its trace formulas and Duke's coefficient bound, Biró's lift, the comparison of adelic and classical half-weight forms, and the interface through which the genus-two kernel of MP.8 reaches BSD.2.
- **MP.8, genus-two similitudes, Jacobi forms and cover-specific Eisenstein analysis.** Integral Fourier-index arithmetic; the Siegel space of degree two, positive similitudes and their square-root double cover; the BFH arithmetic Jacobi realization, genus-two theta series and theta decomposition; the elliptic-newform seed and the Jacobi Eisenstein series; archimedean Whittaker functions, the Novodvorsky transform and the nonvanishing local tests; matrix Möbius inversion, two-cusp unfolding and local Euler factors; and the genuine continuation, constant terms and two-variable polar formula exported to BSD.2.

The proved endpoints are local and global constructions with their source-qualified theorems: the oscillator and metaplectic constructions of Weil and Kudla, Howe duality in the ranges of Gan–Takeda, the Siegel–Weil and Rallis formulas in the ranges of Gan–Qiu–Takeda, the Shimura correspondence and trace formulas of Duke–Imamoḡlu–Tóth, and the genus-two analysis of Bump–Friedberg–Hoffstein. Lafforgue's metaplectic programme is recorded as a programme. Wherever a source's proof was not read, or a supplier does not yet state what is needed, the node says so and a gap records the missing input.

The blueprint has 261 nodes: 176 in part MP.0 and 85 in part MP.8. Every layer is `planned` and none is `closed`: each records gaps (the per-node proof and signature boundaries of part MP.0 among them) or supplier requests, listed under Gaps and Requests.

**What is not here.**

- Local fields, adeles, Haar measures, restricted products and Tamagawa measures: AdelicAlgebraicGroups AA.0–AA.2; Siegel sets and adelic reduction theory: AA.3.
- Schwartz–Bruhat spaces, Fourier transforms, Fourier inversion and Poisson summation: AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors AL.0, with the finite-dimensional, archimedean-joint and oscillatory extensions requested as a Part II of it (R0.1). Local L- and ε-factors and their Tate normalisations: AL.1–AL.3.
- Smooth representations, parabolic induction, Jacquet modules, admissibility and finite length: SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.0, SR.2 and SR.3. Harish-Chandra modules and globalisation: AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups AF.1; automorphic forms, growth, constant terms and cusp decay on linear groups: AF.2 and AF.3; the classical-to-automorphic GL₂ dictionary: AF.5.
- Principal series, Eisenstein series, intertwining operators and spectral theory on linear groups: AutomorphicSpectralTheory AS.0–AS.2. This roadmap proves only their adaptation to the cover.
- Hilbert symbols and local Hasse invariants: Tau Ceti's QuadraticFormInvariants layer 6C. Orthogonal and symplectic groups and their standard representations: Tau Ceti's ClassicalGroups layer 0. Lagrangian complements and symplectic bases: MordellLawrenceVenkatesh LV.3. Finite quadratic modules and discriminant forms: Tau Ceti's Completed IntegralLattices layer 3.
- Classical modular forms, newforms, Atkin–Lehner and Fricke operators, Hecke operators and L-functions: Tau Ceti's ModularForms layers 0, 2, 4, 6 and 7. Whittaker and Bessel functions: QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms QM.2. Genus characters, ideal classes and the arithmetic of binary quadratic forms: GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.2 and GN.3, with the missing arithmetic requested (R0.20, R0.24).
- Waldspurger's formula and the toric periods: GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights GZ.5; incoherent Eisenstein derivatives: GZ.6. Quadratic-twist nonvanishing with prescribed local conditions: RankZeroOneBSD BSD.2. Eta quotients, q-series and mock modular forms: QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms.
- The Shimura–Waldspurger correspondence for Mp₂ₙ, Arthur's multiplicity formula for Mp₂ₙ and finite Weil–Heisenberg representations: the proposed "Metaplectic groups, Weil representations and automorphic theta kernels, Part II" (design job DESIGN-MetaplecticAutomorphicFormsPartII, issue #3389). Weil representations over local fields of odd positive characteristic and global function fields: a Part II proposed by the confirmed finding RT-PAPER-DOR-23/5. Exceptional theta correspondences for G₂: the proposed roadmaps ExceptionalThetaCorrespondencesForG2 and LocalLanglandsCorrespondenceForG2.
- The general doubling method and its local zeta integrals for classical groups: the proposed AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactorsPartIIDoubling. MP.6 plans only the theta-pairing case in Gan–Qiu–Takeda's normalisation (see Boundaries).
- Metaplectic geometric Satake, metaplectic shtukas and their excursion operators: requested as Part II extensions of GeometricSatakeAndFusion GS3 and GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands GS.5 (R0.13, R0.14).

**Suppliers.** These are the prerequisites of the nodes below that lie outside the roadmap; the layers that use each are listed under Dependencies.

- **The pinned libraries.** Mathlib supplies bilinear maps and forms with their isometries, multiplicative type tags, multiplicative 2-cocycles, centers, semidirect products, roots of unity, representation coinvariants, intertwining maps and equivalences, continuous representations, Schwartz functions, quadratic maps and forms with their polarisation and basis expansions, the symplectic and unitary matrix groups, positive-definite matrices, the one- and two-variable Jacobi theta functions, the Gamma function, Γ₀(N), right cosets, the Möbius function, Smith normal form over a PID, the Gaussian integral, one-variable meromorphy and Artinian modules. Tau Ceti supplies the group extension of a factor set (with its inclusion, projection, canonical section, rescaling equivalence and central inclusion for the trivial action), the trivial multiplicative action, the isometry group of a bilinear form and the Cholesky equivalence. - `QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms` asks `MP.6`: The Jacobi theory that the verified finding RT-AREA-automorphic-1/20 gives to MetaplecticAutomorphicForms, planned once and before MP.7: the Jacobi group H(W) ⋊ Sp(W) with its metaplectic cover and unitary analogue, its Schrödinger–Weil representation, Jacobi forms of given weight and index with multiplier systems and cusp conditions, and the theta decomposition. The fix proposes a sub-stage of MP.6 for it (research/blueprint/redteam/RT-AREA-automorphic-1.fixes.md, 'MP.6:jacobi'); the request names MP.6 because that sub-stage is not yet an atlas stage. QM.1 needs the instance in which Sp(W) = SL₂ and the index is a positive definite half-integral n × n matrix F (2F integral with even diagonal), as in Skoruppa, arXiv:0707.0718, §4; QM.1 itself uses n = 1 and F = m. (a) Group. For Γ ≤ SL(2, ℤ), J_n(Γ) = Γ ⋉ (ℤⁿ × ℤⁿ) with (A, (λ, μ))(A′, (λ′, μ′)) = (AA′, (λ, μ)A′ + (λ′, μ′)) and (λ, μ)A = (λa + μc, λb + μd) for A = (a b; c d); the same for Γ ≤ Mp₂(ℤ), acting through its image in SL(2, ℤ); and its relation to the Jacobi group H(W) ⋊ Sp(W), whose lattice points act on functions of index F through J_n(Γ) up to the central scalars of the Heisenberg group. (b) Action. For k ∈ ℤ, the right action of J_n(Γ) on functions φ on ℍ × ℂⁿ: (φ|_{k,F}A)(τ, z) = (cτ + d)^{−k}·e(−cF[z]/(cτ + d))·φ(Aτ, z/(cτ + d)) and (φ|_{k,F}[λ, μ])(τ, z) = e(τF[λ] + 2zᵗFλ)·φ(τ, z + λτ + μ), with F[x] = xᵗFx and e(x) = e^{2πix}; for k ∈ ½ + ℤ the same with (cτ + d)^{−k} replaced by w(τ)^{−2k} for (A, w) ∈ Mp₂(ℤ) (MP.7's group). (c) Forms. For Γ of finite index in Mp₂(ℤ), a finite-dimensional Γ-module V and k ∈ ½ℤ: the space J_{k,F}(Γ, V) of holomorphic φ : ℍ × ℂⁿ → V with φ|_{k,F}g = g·φ for all g ∈ J_n(Γ) (ℤⁿ × ℤⁿ acting trivially on V), such that for every α ∈ Mp₂(ℤ) the function φ|_{k,F}α has a Fourier expansion Σ c(l, r)·q^l·e(zᵗr) over l ∈ ℚ, r ∈ ℤⁿ with 4l − F⁻¹[r] ≥ 0; and its subspace of cusp forms, with 4l − F⁻¹[r] > 0. For V = ℂ(ψ), ψ a character of Mp₂(ℤ), the multiplier in QM.1's sense is v(A) = ψ(A, w_A), w_A the principal branch of (cτ + d)^{1/2}; no value of v(−I) is imposed. (d) Half-integral scalar index, n = 1 and m ∈ ½ + ℤ: a treatment under which Zwegers' ϑ(z; τ) is a Jacobi form of weight 1/2 and index 1/2 with multiplier v_η³. Either of two forms serves: through the centre of the Heisenberg group, where the operators U_m[λ, μ]φ(τ, z) = e(m(λ²τ + 2λz + λμ))·φ(τ, z + λτ + μ) satisfy U_m[X′]∘U_m[X] = e(m(λμ′ − λ′μ))·U_m[X + X′] and (U_m[X]φ)|_{k,m}A = U_m[XA](φ|_{k,m}A) for all real m and X; or through φ(τ, z) ↦ φ(τ, 2z), which multiplies the index by 4, so that ϑ(2z; τ) lies in J_{1/2,2}(Mp₂(ℤ), ℂ(ε³)) with ε(A, w) = η(Aτ)/(w(τ)η(τ)). (e) Theta decomposition, at the level of the Heisenberg group: for each τ, every entire function of z ∈ ℂⁿ invariant under all |_{k,F}[λ, μ] is, uniquely, Σ_{x ∈ ℤⁿ/2Fℤⁿ} h_x·ϑ_{F,x}(τ, z), where ϑ_{F,x}(τ, z) = Σ_{r ∈ ℤⁿ, r ≡ x mod 2Fℤⁿ} e(τF⁻¹[r]/4 + rᵗz); and for Jacobi forms, when Γ acts on V through a finite quotient, the resulting isomorphism J_{k,F}(Γ, V) ≅ M_{k−n/2} ⊗ W(F)* ⊗_{ℂ[Mp₂(ℤ)]} Ind V, where M_κ is the Mp₂(ℤ)-module of modular forms of weight κ on subgroups of finite index and W(F) is the Weil representation of the discriminant module (ℤⁿ/2Fℤⁿ, x ↦ F⁻¹[x]/4) (Skoruppa, Theorem 5). QM.1 does not ask the supplier for, and keeps: the eta and theta multipliers, ϑ(z; τ) and its laws, weak and weakly holomorphic Jacobi forms, the Fourier-coefficient and theta-coefficient integrals, φ_{−2,1}, the heat operators and index raising. (needed by `QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms:QM.1/jacobi-modular-slash`, `QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms:QM.1/jacobi-elliptic-slash`, `QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms:QM.1/jacobi-group-law`, `QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms:QM.1/jacobi-form`, `QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms:QM.1/jacobi-cusp-form`, `QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms:QM.1/jacobi-theta-index`, `QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms:QM.1/theta-decomposition`, `QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms:QM.1/jacobi-rank-one-specialisation`).
- `RankZeroOneBSD--BSD.0` asks `MP.7`: Half-integral-weight metaplectic Eisenstein and Whittaker kernels with ramified local characters and test functions (Friedberg–Hoffstein's construction), with their Fourier coefficient and Euler-factor identities, so that the twist series with arbitrary prescribed local behaviour (split, inert, ramified) at finitely many primes can be formed. (needed by `RankZeroOneBSD:BSD.2/prescribed-local-conditions-value-branch`, `RankZeroOneBSD:BSD.2/twist-series-residue`).

## Conventions

The two parts were written separately and from different sources, and in a few places they write the same object in different coordinates. Node text keeps its packet's notation; this list fixes what the letters mean and how the parts' conventions convert into each other.

- **Heisenberg coordinates.** Part MP.0 writes the Heisenberg group of a bilinear form B : W × W → C as Tau Ceti's factor-set extension E_B, in coefficient-first coordinates (t, x) with (t, x)(s, y) = (t + s + B(x, y), x + y). No division by 2 is needed, so E_B exists in characteristic two. When 2 is invertible and ω is alternating, the Heisenberg group of (W, ω) is E_{½ω}; this formula is valid over ℚ₂, since only the characteristic matters. Kudla and part MP.8 write the space coordinate first: MP.8's H(W) = W × ℝ with (w, t)(w′, t′) = (w + w′, t + t′ + ω(w, w′)/2) is E_{½ω} after the swap (t, w) ↔ (w, t). Polarized coordinates E_{½(B−Bᵀ)} ≃ E_B are `MP.0/polarization-equivalence`.
- **Actions.** Native actions are left actions. Kudla's right action of Sp(W) is converted by x·g = g⁻¹x, and the metaplectic cover uses T_g(w) = wg⁻¹ to compare Rao's coordinates with the native left action (`MP.1/metaplectic-double-cover`). Similitudes act on Siegel space on the left, gZ = (AZ + B)(CZ + D)⁻¹, with J = [[0, −I], [I, 0]] (part MP.8).
- **Additive characters and Fourier transforms.** ψ is a nontrivial continuous unitary character of the local field, or of 𝔸/F globally, with self-dual Haar measures. At a real place ψ(t) = e(t) = exp(2πit); part MP.8 writes ψ_m(t) = e(mt) for the central character of index m. Over ℚ the standard global character has ψ_∞(q) = exp(2πiq) and ψ_f(q) = exp(−2πiq) on the finite adeles, which fixes the phases of ω_L and of its conjugate ρ_L (`MP.4/finite-weil-representation`). The Weil index is defined with the positive Fourier kernel ψ(x·y) (`MP.2/weil-index`); Kudla's long Weyl element w acts by the negative-kernel transform (`MP.2/generator-operators`); Mathlib's Fourier integral has the kernel e(−⟨v, w⟩). Each node names the kernel it uses, and a comparison between two nodes converts by v ↦ −v.
- **Quadratic forms.** A quadratic form q has polar form B_q(x, y) = q(x + y) − q(x) − q(y). The Weil-index formula uses det q = ∏ a_i for q = Σ a_i x_i², not det B_q = 2^d ∏ a_i, and η = ψ/2 with γ(a, η) = γ(η·ax²)/γ(η·x²) (`MP.2/weil-index-identities`). Over ℤ, a native `QuadraticForm ℤ (Fin 2 → ℤ)` is a half-integral symmetric matrix T(Q), with integral diagonal and half-integral off-diagonal entries (`MP.8/quadratic-matrix`). The Hermitian quadratic form of a Hermitian space is q(x) = ½Tr⟨x, x⟩ = ⟨x, x⟩ (`MP.2/hermitian-uncertainty`).
- **Covers and genuineness.** S_ψ is the normalizer extension of Sp(W) by the circle U(1), acting on L²(X) (`MP.1/scalar-normalizer-extension`). λ₂ is its continuous character restricting to z ↦ z² on the circle, and Mp(W) = ker λ₂ is the metaplectic double cover, with kernel μ₂; over ℂ it is Sp(W) × μ₂. A representation, function or form on a cover is *genuine* when the nontrivial central element acts by −1. Part MP.8's positive real cover of GSp₄⁺(ℝ) is built differently, from pairs (g, h) with h continuous on the Siegel space and h(Z)² = d(g, Z) = det(CZ + D)/μ(g) (`MP.8/similitude-cover`); its comparison with Mp(W) for dim W = 4 is part of the cross-part audit below. The adelic cover is the restricted product of the local covers modulo the product-one subgroup of ⊕_v μ₂ (`MP.4/adelic-metaplectic-cover`).
- **Gan–Qiu–Takeda parameters (MP.5, MP.6).** For a type-I pair, dim V = m = m₀ + 2r with r the Witt index, dim W = n, ε₀ ∈ {−1, 0, 1} and d(n) = n + ε₀; s_{m,n} = s₀ = (m − d(n))/2 and ρ_H = (m − r − ε₀)/2. A_k are the Laurent coefficients of the Siegel Eisenstein series at s₀ and B_k those of the regularized theta integral at ρ_H. τ(H) = 1 for orthogonal groups except O(1) and split O(1, 1), where it is 1/2, and τ(H) = 2 for unitary groups (`MP.6/theta-measure-normalizations`).
- **Half-integral weight (MP.7).** Γ = PSL(2, ℤ) in weight zero and Γ₀(4) in weight one half. Weight-one-half forms use the unitary normalisation θ(z) = y^{1/4} Σ_n e(n²z) and the multiplier J(γ, z) = θ(γz)/θ(z) (`MP.7/theta-multiplier`); a holomorphic form f corresponds to y^{k/2}f, and at weight one half the conjugation by y^{1/4} relates the two operator normalisations (`MP.7/plus-normalization-conjugation`). The weight-one-half Laplacian has eigenvalue λ = 1/4 + (r/2)², so the spectral parameter is r/2 in weight one half and r in weight zero, and the Whittaker functions are W_{sgn(n)/4, ir/2}(4π|n|y). The plus space is cut out by n ≡ 0, 1 mod 4, with pr⁺ = (2/3)WU + 1/3. Weight-zero forms are φ(z) = 2y^{1/2} Σ_{n≠0} a(n)K_{ir}(2π|n|y)e(nx) with a(1) = 1. The Petersson product is ⟨F, F⟩ = ∫_{Γ₀(4)\ℍ} |F|² dμ, not divided by the area. Fractional powers of a discriminant are powers of |D|. The cycle C_Q runs from z to γ_Q z (clockwise on S_Q when a > 0), the orientation under which Duke–Imamoḡlu–Tóth's Lemma 5 holds; source issue E-DUKE-IMAMOGLU-TOTH-16-E28 records the sign. Biró uses the negative Laplacian, with eigenvalue λ = −1/4 − t².
- **Bump–Friedberg–Hoffstein data (MP.8).** f is a normalised newform of even weight k ≥ 2, trivial character and conductor M; N is an auxiliary level with 8M | N; the index m satisfies N | m and 4m | N², and a = m/N. The cusp j ∈ {0, 1} carries c = N^{1−j}. The auxiliary transform f̂(τ) = τ^{−k} f(−1/(Nτ)) uses N, while the Fricke involution and the completed L-function of f use M (source issue E-MP8-3). K = Sp₄(ℝ) ∩ O₄(ℝ) ≅ U(2) and scalar test coefficients have the form φ(κ) = T(vσ(κ)). The Siegel parameter is s; the normalised inducing exponent is ν = s − 2 and the Weyl reflection is s ↦ 4 − s. Whittaker functions carry a sign ε ∈ {+1, −1, 0}, where 0 is the degenerate W⁰.
- **References to extraction items.** Some MP.7 statements refer to "item N". This is extraction item `PAPER-DUKE-IMAMOGLU-TOTH-16/N` of the reviewed paper routing (`research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-DUKE-IMAMOGLU-TOTH-16.result.json`). Items 80, 100, 109, 119, 120, 122 and 123 are the nodes that list them under Source items; item 93 (the Poincaré residue theorem) and item 105 (the weight-two Poincaré one-form) are routed to AutomorphicSpectralTheory, which those nodes cite as AS.0; item 151 (the Rankin–Selberg norm of a normalised Maass form) is routed to AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors.
- **Locators.** "PDF n" is the physical page of the file whose hash is recorded; "printed n" is the page number on the page. The BFH scan has a cover sheet, so its PDF page index is the printed page minus 542.
- **Prototype boundaries.** 75 nodes of part MP.0 carry the standard boundary of a native signature fragment: *"This is a native signature fragment. The full source hypotheses and missing supplier carriers remain mandatory in the packet; no theorem for arbitrary choices of the displayed parameters is claimed."* Their node sections say "the standard native-fragment boundary"; every other boundary, and every MP.8 signature omission, is printed in full.
- **Identifiers and names.** Node ids are `MetaplecticAutomorphicForms:<layer>/<slug>` and are written below without the roadmap prefix. The display groups `MP.3:towers`, `MP.7:shimura` and so on are headings of this document only; node ids and stages are unchanged. Gaps and requests are numbered here in packet order: G0.n and R0.n for part MP.0, G8.n and R8.n for part MP.8. Each node's **Library** line gives the module and namespace its packet proposes: `TauCeti.Metaplectic.Heisenberg` for the twelve algebraic Heisenberg nodes, `TauCeti.Metaplectic` for the rest of part MP.0 (in modules `TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Metaplectic/Stage0` to `Stage7`) and `TauCeti.Jacobi.GenusTwo` for part MP.8. The suggested Lean file keeps these namespaces.

## Sources

Every statement below is taken from these sources, at the versions recorded. The two parts give the Inventiones paper of Bump, Friedberg and Hoffstein different source ids (`BFH90Invent` in part MP.0, `BFH90` in part MP.8); this list groups the ids by file, using the SHA-256 of the version read, and gives the sections each part read. Excerpts in the node sections are quoted literally from the version named, and the reviews checked them there: REV-MetaplecticAutomorphicForms--MP.0 fetched all 25 recorded PDFs, matched their hashes and checked the 186 node citations at their pages, and REV-MetaplecticAutomorphicForms--MP.8 read the BFH scan throughout. The primary sources are Weil's 1964 Acta paper and Kudla's notes on the local theta correspondence (MP.0–MP.4), Gan–Qiu–Takeda (MP.5–MP.6), Duke–Imamoḡlu–Tóth 2011 and 2016 and Biró (MP.7), and Bump–Friedberg–Hoffstein (MP.7–MP.8); the papers routed to this roadmap by the paper jobs supply the remaining targets of MP.2–MP.7.

- **Stephen S. Kudla, *Notes on the local theta correspondence*.** Unpublished author notes; introduction dated July 6, 1996; 110-page author copy.

## What the pinned libraries have

These are the 85 declarations of the pinned libraries that the nodes cite (58 in part MP.0 and 28 in part MP.8; `SemidirectProduct` is cited by both). Each was read at Mathlib `082e2d37e8b0463410cdb532e111cd43d5a66174` or Tau Ceti `f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369` by its part's planner and again by its reviewer. A near miss is not a baseline declaration: the boundary declarations (the symplectic matrix group, the semidirect product, one-variable meromorphy, continuous representations) are cited for what they provide, and the nodes that need more say so.

**`Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Invertible/Defs.lean`**

- `mathlib:invOf_mul_self` (theorem; part MP.0): The chosen inverse of an invertible element multiplied by it is one.

**`Mathlib/Algebra/Group/TypeTags/Basic.lean`**

- `mathlib:Multiplicative` (def; part MP.0): Existing multiplicative view of an additive group; no new additive central-extension type is needed.

**`Mathlib/Algebra/GroupWithZero/Defs.lean`**

- `mathlib:mul_left_cancel₀` (theorem; part MP.8): Cancel a nonzero left factor; applied in Z to 4a and 2a.

**`Mathlib/Analysis/Distribution/SchwartzSpace/Basic.lean`**

- `mathlib:SchwartzMap` (structure; part MP.0): Native real smooth functions with all polynomially weighted derivative seminorm bounds.

**`Mathlib/Analysis/Meromorphic/Basic.lean`**

- `mathlib:MeromorphicOn` (def; part MP.8): Pointwise meromorphic-at predicate on a set in a nontrivially normed field. It supplies scalar one-complex-variable slices, not a two-complex-variable meromorphic API.

**`Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Gamma/Basic.lean`**

- `mathlib:Complex.Gamma` (def; part MP.0): Complex Gamma using the analytically continued auxiliary definition; poles and argument conventions are retained.

**`Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Gaussian/GaussianIntegral.lean`**

- `mathlib:integrable_exp_neg_mul_sq` (theorem; part MP.8): Root-namespace integrability of exp(−b x²) for b>0, needed before Gaussian Fubini and change of variables.
- `mathlib:integral_gaussian` (theorem; part MP.8): Root-namespace real Gaussian integral ∫ exp(−b x²)=√(π/b); positive b gives the analytic formula used after Cholesky/Fubini.

**`Mathlib/Data/Int/ModEq.lean`**

- `mathlib:Int.ModEq` (def; part MP.8): Congruence of integers modulo an integer, including negative and zero moduli.
- `mathlib:Int.modEq_iff_dvd` (theorem; part MP.8): R_i≡R′_i modulo 2a iff 2a divides R′_i−R_i, giving the integral shift parameter.

**`Mathlib/GroupTheory/Coset/Defs.lean`**

- `mathlib:QuotientGroup.rightRel` (def; part MP.0): Right-coset setoid y*x⁻¹∈H. Its quotient supplies H\G in the Poincaré sum.

**`Mathlib/GroupTheory/SemidirectProduct.lean`**

- `mathlib:SemidirectProduct` (structure; parts MP.0, MP.8): Native semidirect-product carrier and group law for an action by multiplicative automorphisms.

**`Mathlib/GroupTheory/Subgroup/Center.lean`**

- `mathlib:Subgroup.mem_center_iff` (theorem; part MP.0): An element belongs to the center iff it commutes with every group element.

**`Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/BilinearForm/Basic.lean`**

- `mathlib:LinearMap.BilinForm.flip` (abbrev; part MP.0): The native transposed bilinear form.
- `mathlib:LinearMap.BilinForm.flip_apply` (theorem; part MP.0): The transpose evaluates to B(y,x).

**`Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/BilinearForm/IsometryEquiv.lean`**

- `mathlib:LinearMap.BilinForm.IsometryEquiv` (structure; part MP.0): A linear equivalence between two modules preserving the given scalar-valued forms.
- `mathlib:LinearMap.BilinForm.IsometryEquiv.map_app` (theorem; part MP.0): Exact equality expressing preservation of the forms.
- `mathlib:LinearMap.BilinForm.IsometryEquiv.refl` (def; part MP.0): Identity isometry.
- `mathlib:LinearMap.BilinForm.IsometryEquiv.symm` (def; part MP.0): Inverse isometry.
- `mathlib:LinearMap.BilinForm.IsometryEquiv.trans` (def; part MP.0): Composition of isometries.

**`Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/BilinearForm/Properties.lean`**

- `mathlib:LinearMap.BilinForm.IsAlt` (def; part MP.0): The native alternating predicate: the diagonal values vanish.
- `mathlib:LinearMap.BilinForm.IsAlt.neg_eq` (theorem; part MP.0): An alternating bilinear form satisfies −B(y,x)=B(x,y), over the stated ring hypotheses.
- `mathlib:LinearMap.BilinForm.Nondegenerate` (abbrev; part MP.0): The native nondegeneracy predicate, including separation in each variable.

**`Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/BilinearMap.lean`**

- `mathlib:LinearMap.BilinForm` (abbrev; part MP.0): The scalar-valued specialization of the native bilinear-map type.
- `mathlib:LinearMap.BilinMap` (abbrev; part MP.0): Bilinear maps W×W→C over a common scalar ring, allowing the coefficient module to differ from W and R.
- `mathlib:LinearMap.domRestrict₁₂` (def; part MP.0): Restrict both arguments of a bilinear map to a submodule, keeping its coefficient module.
- `mathlib:LinearMap.map_add₂` (theorem; part MP.0): Additivity in the first input with both arguments displayed; second-input additivity is native linear-map additivity.
- `mathlib:LinearMap.restrictScalars₁₂` (def; part MP.0): Restrict the scalar ring on a bilinear map without changing its values.

**`Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/FreeModule/PID.lean`**

- `mathlib:Submodule.exists_smith_normal_form_of_le` (theorem; part MP.8): For submodules N≤O of a finite free module over a PID, obtains bases with each N-basis vector a_i times an O-basis vector. The statement does not itself impose a_i|a_j; the binary content/product argument fixes the needed ordered invariants.

**`Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/BilinearForm.lean`**

- `mathlib:Matrix.toBilin'` (def; part MP.0): The matrix bilinear form x,y↦Σ xᵢMᵢⱼyⱼ, used directly in the tests.
- `mathlib:Matrix.toBilin'_apply` (theorem; part MP.0): Explicit finite-sum evaluation of that matrix form.

**`Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/PosDef.lean`**

- `mathlib:Matrix.PosDef` (def; part MP.8): Hermitian matrix with strictly positive finitely supported quadratic evaluation; over finite real indices this gives positive dot-product evaluation on every nonzero vector.

**`Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/ToLin.lean`**

- `mathlib:Matrix.toLin'` (def; part MP.8): Native linear equivalence from a finite matrix to its coordinate linear map, evaluating as multiplication of the matrix by a column vector.
- `mathlib:dotProductBilin` (def; part MP.8): The coordinate dot product packaged as a bilinear map; fixing R∈Z² gives the linear functional x↦R·x. This declaration is in the root namespace.

**`Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/QuadraticForm/Basic.lean`**

- `mathlib:QuadraticForm` (abbrev; part MP.8): Native scalar-valued quadratic maps; over Z on Z² these encode integral binary quadratic polynomials, hence half-integral symmetric matrices.
- `mathlib:QuadraticMap` (structure; part MP.8): Native quadratic maps with degree-two scaling and a bilinear companion.
- `mathlib:QuadraticMap.congr_fun` (theorem; part MP.8): Equality of quadratic maps implies equality at every input.
- `mathlib:QuadraticMap.ext` (theorem; part MP.8): Quadratic forms are equal if their values are equal on every vector.
- `mathlib:QuadraticMap.linMulLin` (def; part MP.8): The product of two linear forms is a native quadratic map.
- `mathlib:QuadraticMap.linMulLin_apply` (theorem; part MP.8): The product quadratic map evaluates to the product of the two linear-form values.
- `mathlib:QuadraticMap.map_smul` (theorem; part MP.8): A quadratic map sends a·x to a² times its value at x.
- `mathlib:QuadraticMap.proj` (def; part MP.8): The native coordinate quadratic form x↦x_i x_j, used in mixed-term tests.
- `mathlib:QuadraticMap.proj_apply` (theorem; part MP.8): Coordinate quadratic-form evaluation is x_i x_j.

**`Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/QuadraticForm/Basis.lean`**

- `mathlib:QuadraticMap.sum_repr_sq_add_sum_repr_mul_polar` (theorem; part MP.8): A quadratic map expands in diagonal basis values and unordered off-diagonal polar terms, without assuming that 2 is invertible.
- `mathlib:QuadraticMap.toBilin` (def; part MP.8): An ordered basis gives an upper-triangular bilinear representative over Z; symmetry and division by 2 are not required.
- `mathlib:QuadraticMap.toQuadraticMap_toBilin` (theorem; part MP.8): The quadratic map of the ordered-basis bilinear representative is the original map.

**`Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/SymplecticGroup.lean`**

- `mathlib:Matrix.symplecticGroup` (def; part MP.8): Boundary only: matrices satisfying AJAᵀ=J, as a submonoid. This is neither a similitude group nor its double cover.

**`Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/UnitaryGroup.lean`**

- `mathlib:Matrix.unitaryGroup` (abbrev; part MP.8): Native unitary matrices as a submonoid with a group structure; specializes to U(2) without re-planning compact-group structure.

**`Mathlib/NumberTheory/ArithmeticFunction/Moebius.lean`**

- `mathlib:ArithmeticFunction.moebius` (def; part MP.8): Integer-valued scalar Möbius function: (−1)^cardFactors for squarefree n, otherwise zero; μ₂ uses it on positive Smith coefficients.

**`Mathlib/NumberTheory/ModularForms/CongruenceSubgroups.lean`**

- `mathlib:CongruenceSubgroup.Gamma0` (def; part MP.0): Native subgroup of SL₂(Z) with lower-left entry zero mod N.

**`Mathlib/NumberTheory/ModularForms/JacobiTheta/TwoVariable.lean`**

- `mathlib:jacobiTheta₂` (def; part MP.8): The native two-variable classical theta sum Σ_n exp(2πinz+πin²τ); the genus-two diagonal test reduces to two such sums.

**`Mathlib/RepresentationTheory/Coinvariants.lean`**

- `mathlib:Representation.Coinvariants` (def; part MP.0): The algebraic module quotient by the span of ρ(g)v−v; no smooth-category assertion.
- `mathlib:Representation.Coinvariants.lift` (def; part MP.0): A linear map satisfying f∘ρ(g)=f descends uniquely to the quotient.
- `mathlib:Representation.Coinvariants.mk` (def; part MP.0): Native quotient linear map onto the algebraic coinvariants.

**`Mathlib/RepresentationTheory/Continuous/Basic.lean`**

- `mathlib:ContRepresentation` (structure; part MP.0): A monoid homomorphism into continuous linear endomorphisms. It imposes no continuity of the group parameter.
- `mathlib:ContRepresentation.toRepresentation` (abbrev; part MP.0): Underlying algebraic representation of a continuous-operator representation.

**`Mathlib/RepresentationTheory/Homological/GroupCohomology/LowDegree.lean`**

- `mathlib:groupCohomology.IsMulCocycle₂` (def; part MP.0): The multiplicative cocycle identity used by FactorSet.

**`Mathlib/RepresentationTheory/Intertwining.lean`**

- `mathlib:Representation.Equiv` (structure; part MP.0): An equivariant linear equivalence of native algebraic representations.
- `mathlib:Representation.IntertwiningMap` (structure; part MP.0): Linear map with the exact equivariance condition.

**`Mathlib/RingTheory/Artinian/Defs.lean`**

- `mathlib:IsArtinian` (abbrev; part MP.0): Well-founded strict submodule order; finite-length theta modules need the separate smooth-category theorem.

**`Mathlib/RingTheory/RootsOfUnity/Basic.lean`**

- `mathlib:rootsOfUnity` (def; part MP.0): The subgroup of units satisfying ζ^n=1; at n=2,C this is μ₂.

**`TauCeti/GroupTheory/GroupExtension/Of/FactorSet.lean`**

- `tauceti:TauCeti.FactorSet` (structure; part MP.0): Normalized multiplicative two-cocycle for a specified coefficient action.
- `tauceti:TauCeti.FactorSet.Extension` (structure; part MP.0): Native carrier with left coefficient and right group coordinates; its group instance uses the factor set.
- `tauceti:TauCeti.FactorSet.Extension.inv_left` (theorem; part MP.0): The coefficient coordinate of the inverse is the native factor-set inverse formula.
- `tauceti:TauCeti.FactorSet.Extension.inv_right` (theorem; part MP.0): The quotient coordinate of the inverse is x.right inverse.
- `tauceti:TauCeti.FactorSet.Extension.mul_left` (theorem; part MP.0): The coefficient coordinate of a product is x.left·(x.right acting on y.left)·α(x.right,y.right).
- `tauceti:TauCeti.FactorSet.Extension.mul_right` (theorem; part MP.0): The quotient coordinate of a product is x.right·y.right.
- `tauceti:TauCeti.FactorSet.canonicalSection` (def; part MP.0): Canonical set-theoretic section with coefficient coordinate one; it is not generally a homomorphism.
- `tauceti:TauCeti.FactorSet.groupExtension` (def; part MP.0): Packages the preceding native maps as a group extension.
- `tauceti:TauCeti.FactorSet.inl` (def; part MP.0): Canonical injection of coefficients into the extension.
- `tauceti:TauCeti.FactorSet.inl_injective` (theorem; part MP.0): The coefficient injection is injective.
- `tauceti:TauCeti.FactorSet.inl_mul_canonicalSection` (theorem; part MP.0): Every extension element is its central coordinate times the section of its quotient coordinate.
- `tauceti:TauCeti.FactorSet.inl_range_le_center` (theorem; part MP.0): For the trivial coefficient action the coefficient subgroup lies in the center.
- `tauceti:TauCeti.FactorSet.range_inl_eq_ker_rightHom` (theorem; part MP.0): Exactness at the extension.
- `tauceti:TauCeti.FactorSet.rescaleEquiv` (def; part MP.0): A cochain satisfying α(g,h)x(gh)=β(g,h)(g acting on x(h)·x(g)) gives an equivalence of group extensions, multiplying the coefficient by x(g).
- `tauceti:TauCeti.FactorSet.rescaleEquiv_apply` (theorem; part MP.0): Coordinate formula for the forward rescaling equivalence.
- `tauceti:TauCeti.FactorSet.rescaleEquiv_symm_apply` (theorem; part MP.0): The inverse equivalence divides the coefficient by the cochain.
- `tauceti:TauCeti.FactorSet.rightHom` (def; part MP.0): Canonical projection of the extension to its quotient group.
- `tauceti:TauCeti.FactorSet.rightHom_surjective` (theorem; part MP.0): Surjectivity of the quotient projection.

**`TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/BilinearForm/Isometry.lean`**

- `tauceti:TauCeti.BilinForm.isometryGroup` (def; part MP.0): Subgroup of linear automorphisms preserving a bilinear form; available over any commutative semiring, without a new symplectic-space wrapper.
- `tauceti:TauCeti.BilinForm.isometryGroupEquivIsometryEquiv` (def; part MP.0): Equivalence from the subgroup carrier to native self-isometries.
- `tauceti:TauCeti.BilinForm.mem_isometryGroup` (theorem; part MP.0): Membership is preservation of every bilinear value.

**`TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/Cholesky/Equiv.lean`**

- `tauceti:TauCeti.choleskyEquiv` (def; part MP.8): Equivalence of real positive-definite matrices with lower triangular matrices of positive diagonal, with LLᵀ as Gram map and uniqueness. Reverse the two coordinate indices to obtain the BFH upper-triangular Q with Y=QQᵀ.

**`TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/ProjectiveRepresentation/Extension.lean`**

- `tauceti:TauCeti.trivialMulDistribMulAction` (def; part MP.0): The existing trivial action through the identity automorphism, installed only locally.
- `tauceti:TauCeti.trivialMulDistribMulAction_smul` (theorem; part MP.0): Every group element acts identically under that action.

<a id="mp0"></a>
## MP.0 — Symplectic and Heisenberg groups with topology

*Part MP.0; coverage `planned`; 18 nodes, 4 planets; 4 remaining items, each recorded as a gap below.*

The layer has two halves. The first is algebra over an arbitrary commutative ring R: the Heisenberg group of a bilinear form B is not built anew but is Tau Ceti's `FactorSet.Extension` of the bilinear factor set, so its group law, exact sequence, central inclusion and canonical section are library declarations. On top of it the layer proves the inverse and commutator formulas, the center criterion and, for B = ½ω with ω alternating and nondegenerate and 2 invertible, that the center is exactly the image of the coefficients; it transports isometries to automorphisms, passes between B and its antisymmetrisation by the quadratic correction ½B(x, x), and extends a central character along the canonical section exactly when it kills every B(x, y). These twelve nodes were planned first, on 27 September, and the review verified all twelve.

The second half is analysis over a local field of characteristic zero: the transported topology, the product Haar measure, the Schrödinger model ρ_ψ on Schwartz–Bruhat functions of a Lagrangian X (locally constant compactly supported at finite places, the joint real Schwartz space at infinity), its realisation as a compactly induced representation, the Hilbert model on L²(X) and the identification of its smooth vectors with S(X). Lagrangian complements come from MordellLawrenceVenkatesh LV.3; the vector-space Fourier analysis, self-dual measures and joint archimedean Schwartz spaces come from AL.0, whose finite-dimensional extension is requested (R0.1). Four of the six analytic nodes record their proof and signature boundaries as gaps (G0.1–G0.4).

The reviewer corrected `MP.0/topological-heisenberg` (continuity of the isometry action needs jointly continuous evaluation). Its findings on this layer's suggested signatures remain open: a translated Dirac measure satisfies the stated Haar signature, a representation of ℤ on ℂ by 2^n satisfies the stated unitarity signature, and the Hilbert model's zero-space test equates one fixed operator with every character.

### MP.0:heisenberg-algebra — The bilinear Heisenberg extension

<a id="mp0-bilinear-factor-set"></a>
#### Bilinear Heisenberg factor set

`MP.0/bilinear-factor-set` · construction · planet “Heisenberg group” · part MP.0

Construct α_B(x,y)=B(x,y), viewed multiplicatively, as a native normalized factor set on Multiplicative W with coefficients Multiplicative C and trivial action. Its existing extension E_B has multiplication (t,x)(s,y)=(t+s+B(x,y),x+y). The maps t↦(t,0) and (t,x)↦x and their exactness are the native inl, rightHom and groupExtension.

**Hypotheses.**

- R is a commutative ring; W and C are additive commutative groups and R-modules. B:W×W→C is a native R-bilinear map.
- Write E_B for the existing FactorSet.Extension of the bilinear factor set. This is notation, not a proposed wrapper. Coordinates are (t,w), coefficient first; identity is (0,0). The coefficient action is the native trivial action.

**Construction.**

1. Bilinearity gives B(x+y,z)+B(x,y)=B(y,z)+B(x,y+z), the native multiplicative cocycle identity after type tagging and using the trivial action.
2. B(0,0)=0 gives normalization. Supply these two fields to FactorSet; use its existing group instance, exact sequence, section and central inclusion without rebuilding them.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.Metaplectic.Heisenberg.bilinearFactorSet_apply` (simp): The additive value of α_B(x,y) is B(x,y).
- `TauCeti.Metaplectic.Heisenberg.bilinearFactorSet_mul_left` (projection): The coefficient coordinate of pq is t+s+B(x,y).
- `TauCeti.Metaplectic.Heisenberg.bilinearFactorSet_mul_right` (projection): The quotient coordinate of pq is x+y.

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.Metaplectic.Heisenberg.bilinearFactorSet_zero` (degenerate): For B=0 on W=C=Z, the coefficient coordinate of pq is t+s.
- `TauCeti.Metaplectic.Heisenberg.bilinearFactorSet_cross` (computation): For W=Z² and B(x,y)=x₀y₁, α_B(e₀,e₁)=1 in additive coefficient coordinates.
- `TauCeti.Metaplectic.Heisenberg.bilinearFactorSet_reversed` (non-example): For the same native matrix form, α_B(e₁,e₀)=0. Replacing B by its transpose fails the two ordered tests.

**Acceptance.**

- No division by 2 is used; the construction works in characteristic two.
- For C=R and B=½ω, with ω alternating and 2 invertible, the multiplication is exactly Kudla’s convention after swapping the written coordinate order.
- For B=0 the native multiplication is addition on C×W.

**Uses.**

- Kudla I.1, p.3; MP.0–1: Provide the exact Heisenberg group and central embedding before choosing a smooth representation.
- Weil I.§§3–4, pp.148–149; MP.0 and MP.8: Support polarized bilinear cocycles and the Heisenberg input to Jacobi semidirect products.
- Kudla I.2, p.6: Allow a lattice domain over Z with coefficient module in the ambient local field; no division operation on the lattice is assumed.

<a id="mp0-inverse"></a>
#### Inverse in the bilinear extension

`MP.0/inverse` · lemma · part MP.0

For p=(t,x) in E_B, p⁻¹=(−t+B(x,x),−x).

**Hypotheses.**

- R is a commutative ring; W and C are additive commutative groups and R-modules. B:W×W→C is a native R-bilinear map.
- Write E_B for the existing FactorSet.Extension of the bilinear factor set. This is notation, not a proposed wrapper. Coordinates are (t,w), coefficient first; identity is (0,0). The coefficient action is the native trivial action.

**Proof outline.**

1. Specialize the native inverse coordinate formulas to the trivial action. Bilinearity gives B(x,−x)=−B(x,x); simplify coefficient inversion into additive negation.
2. Alternatively multiply the proposed inverse on either side using the native product formulas; both coordinates are zero.

**Acceptance.**

- For B=0 the inverse is ordinary negation.
- For B(x,y)=x₀y₁ over Z and p=(0,(2,3)), the inverse has coefficient 6, not 0.
- For an alternating B the diagonal correction vanishes.

<a id="mp0-commutator"></a>
#### Commutator in a bilinear central extension

`MP.0/commutator` · lemma · part MP.0

For p=(t,x),q=(s,y), with commutator convention pqp⁻¹q⁻¹, the commutator is inl(B(x,y)−B(y,x)).

**Hypotheses.**

- R is a commutative ring; W and C are additive commutative groups and R-modules. B:W×W→C is a native R-bilinear map.
- Write E_B for the existing FactorSet.Extension of the bilinear factor set. This is notation, not a proposed wrapper. Coordinates are (t,w), coefficient first; identity is (0,0). The coefficient action is the native trivial action.

**Proof outline.**

1. Substitute inverse and the native multiplication coordinate formulas into the fourfold product.
2. The quotient coordinate is zero. Expand B(x+y,−x) and B(y,−y) by bilinearity; diagonal terms cancel and the coefficient becomes B(x,y)−B(y,x). Identify the resulting pair with native inl.

- The coefficient does not depend on t or s.
- For B(x,y)=x₀y₁ and x=e₀,y=e₁ over Z, the commutator is central 1.
- The same triangular form over Z/2Z is noncommutative; the generic bilinear construction still applies.

<a id="mp0-center-criterion"></a>
#### Center criterion for a bilinear extension

`MP.0/center-criterion` · lemma · part MP.0

An element (t,x) belongs to the center of E_B iff B(x,y)=B(y,x) for every y∈W.

**Hypotheses.**

- R is a commutative ring; W and C are additive commutative groups and R-modules. B:W×W→C is a native R-bilinear map.
- Write E_B for the existing FactorSet.Extension of the bilinear factor set. This is notation, not a proposed wrapper. Coordinates are (t,w), coefficient first; identity is (0,0). The coefficient action is the native trivial action.

**Proof outline.**

1. Use Subgroup.mem_center_iff. Compare (t,x)(s,y) and (s,y)(t,x) using the native product coordinates.
2. The quotient coordinates agree. Cancel t+s in C; this leaves precisely equality of the two bilinear values. For necessity it suffices to take s=0; for sufficiency allow arbitrary s.

**Acceptance.**

- For symmetric B the entire group is central.
- For B=0 on Z the center strictly contains the coefficient subgroup, detected by (0,1).
- The criterion uses the radical of B−Bᵀ and does not assume 2 invertible.

<a id="mp0-half-form-commutator"></a>
#### Commutator for the half-alternating convention

`MP.0/half-form-commutator` · lemma · part MP.0

Let ω be alternating and let 2 be invertible in R. In E_{½ω}, pqp⁻¹q⁻¹=inl(ω(x,y)).

**Hypotheses.**

- R is a commutative ring and W,W′,W″ are R-modules with additive commutative groups. Forms are native scalar-valued bilinear forms, with no nondegeneracy assumption unless explicitly stated.
- E_B denotes the same native extension, with coordinates (t,w). Maps between extensions fix the coefficient coordinate.
- ω is alternating; 2 is invertible in R.

**Proof outline.**

1. Apply commutator to B=½ω. Native IsAlt.neg_eq gives ω(y,x)=−ω(x,y).
2. The coefficient is ½(ω(x,y)−ω(y,x))=ω(x,y), using invOf_mul_self for 2.

**Acceptance.**

- For the standard alternating form over Q, the two standard basis vectors have commutator central 1.
- No residue-characteristic restriction occurs: the field Q₂ has invertible 2.
- The convention p⁻¹q⁻¹pq must not be substituted into a calculation using a different bracket convention without checking the resulting identity.

<a id="mp0-half-form-center"></a>
#### Center of the Heisenberg group

`MP.0/half-form-center` · theorem · part MP.0

If ω is alternating and nondegenerate and 2 is invertible in R, the center of E_{½ω} is exactly the range of its native coefficient injection.

**Hypotheses.**

- R is a commutative ring and W,W′,W″ are R-modules with additive commutative groups. Forms are native scalar-valued bilinear forms, with no nondegeneracy assumption unless explicitly stated.
- E_B denotes the same native extension, with coordinates (t,w). Maps between extensions fix the coefficient coordinate.
- ω is alternating and nondegenerate; 2 is invertible in R.

**Proof outline.**

1. Native centrality of inl gives one inclusion. For a central (t,x), half-form-commutator and injectivity of inl imply ω(x,y)=0 for every y.
2. Apply the separation property in native Nondegenerate to obtain x=0. The element is then inl(t), proving the other inclusion.

**Acceptance.**

- A zero form on a nonzero module violates nondegeneracy and has a larger center.
- For the zero module the statement still identifies the whole extension with its coefficient subgroup.
- No finite-dimensionality, topology, or field hypothesis is used in this algebraic theorem.

<a id="mp0-isometry-extension"></a>
#### Extension isomorphism induced by an isometry

`MP.0/isometry-extension` · construction · part MP.0

For scalar forms B on W and D on W′ and a native isometry e:B≃D, construct the group isomorphism E_B≃E_D sending (t,x) to (t,e(x)).

**Hypotheses.**

- R is a commutative ring and W,W′,W″ are R-modules with additive commutative groups. Forms are native scalar-valued bilinear forms, with no nondegeneracy assumption unless explicitly stated.
- E_B denotes the same native extension, with coordinates (t,w). Maps between extensions fix the coefficient coordinate.

**Construction.**

1. Use the underlying linear equivalence on the quotient coordinate and identity on the coefficient coordinate, with e inverse giving the inverse map.
2. Preservation of multiplication follows from linear additivity and native IsometryEquiv.map_app: D(e(x),e(y))=B(x,y).

**API.**

- `TauCeti.Metaplectic.Heisenberg.extensionIsometry_apply` (projection): The coordinate formula is (t,x)↦(t,e(x)).
- `TauCeti.Metaplectic.Heisenberg.extensionIsometry_refl` (functoriality): The identity native isometry gives the identity group isomorphism.
- `TauCeti.Metaplectic.Heisenberg.extensionIsometry_trans` (functoriality): Extension of the composite f∘e is extension of f composed with extension of e, with the same order as native IsometryEquiv.trans.
- `TauCeti.Metaplectic.Heisenberg.extensionIsometry_inl` (compatibility): Extension of e sends inl_B(t) to inl_D(t).

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.Metaplectic.Heisenberg.extensionIsometry_identity` (computation): The identity isometry of the zero form on Z fixes (3,4).
- `TauCeti.Metaplectic.Heisenberg.extensionIsometry_negation` (computation): Negation preserves any scalar bilinear form on Z and sends (3,4) to (3,−4), preserving the coefficient 3.
- `TauCeti.Metaplectic.Heisenberg.extensionIsometry_inverse` (compatibility): Extension of the native inverse isometry undoes extension of e, including when the underlying modules differ.

**Acceptance.**

- Different underlying modules are allowed.
- The map fixes the native central injection pointwise.
- Applied to half an alternating form, this supplies the symplectic automorphisms in Kudla p.3.

**Uses.**

- Kudla I.1, p.3; MP.0: Transport Heisenberg coordinates under symplectic isometries.
- Kudla I.2, pp.7–9; MP.0–1: Compare polarizations and conjugate induced models while preserving their central character.

<a id="mp0-isometry-action"></a>
#### Isometry action on the Heisenberg group

`MP.0/isometry-action` · construction · planet “Symplectic action” · part MP.0

For a scalar form B, construct a group homomorphism from the native TauCeti.BilinForm.isometryGroup B to automorphisms of E_B, sending e to (t,x)↦(t,e(x)).

**Hypotheses.**

- R is a commutative ring and W,W′,W″ are R-modules with additive commutative groups. Forms are native scalar-valued bilinear forms, with no nondegeneracy assumption unless explicitly stated.
- E_B denotes the same native extension, with coordinates (t,w). Maps between extensions fix the coefficient coordinate.

**Construction.**

1. Use the native equivalence from the isometry subgroup to self-isometries and the preceding extension construction.
2. Verify the identity and multiplication laws by the coordinate formula, using the left-composition convention of linear automorphisms. No projective scalar ambiguity occurs in this action on the Heisenberg group.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.Metaplectic.Heisenberg.extensionIsometryAction_apply` (projection): The group element e acts by (t,x)↦(t,e(x)).
- `TauCeti.Metaplectic.Heisenberg.extensionIsometryAction_inl` (compatibility): Every e fixes each inl(t).
- `TauCeti.Metaplectic.Heisenberg.extensionIsometryAction_injective` (characterisation): The action homomorphism is injective: evaluation on all (0,x) determines e.

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.Metaplectic.Heisenberg.extensionIsometryAction_identity` (computation): The native group identity for the zero form on Z fixes (3,4).
- `TauCeti.Metaplectic.Heisenberg.extensionIsometryAction_negation` (non-example): The negation element of the native isometry group of the zero form on Z sends (3,4) to (3,−4); a constant identity action fails.
- `TauCeti.Metaplectic.Heisenberg.extensionIsometryAction_center` (compatibility): Every native isometry-group element fixes the native coefficient injection, for all t.

**Acceptance.**

- This is an honest action on E_B; it does not construct an honest symplectic action on an irreducible representation space.
- The action is faithful, including degenerate forms: equality on (0,x) recovers the linear automorphism.
- Kudla uses a right action; translate it by x·e=e⁻¹(x) before comparing multiplication order.

**Uses.**

- Kudla I.1, pp.3–4; MP.1: Supply the group automorphism used to twist the irreducible Heisenberg representation before choosing an intertwiner.
- MetaplecticAutomorphicForms:MP.8: Supply the symplectic part of a Jacobi action. The similitude action that scales the center is an additional MP.8 obligation.

<a id="mp0-polarization-cocycle"></a>
#### Quadratic correction between Heisenberg cocycles

`MP.0/polarization-cocycle` · lemma · part MP.0

For scalar B and invertible 2, put q(x)=½B(x,x) and ω=B−Bᵀ. Then ½ω(x,y)+q(x+y)=B(x,y)+q(x)+q(y).

**Hypotheses.**

- R is a commutative ring and W,W′,W″ are R-modules with additive commutative groups. Forms are native scalar-valued bilinear forms, with no nondegeneracy assumption unless explicitly stated.
- E_B denotes the same native extension, with coordinates (t,w). Maps between extensions fix the coefficient coordinate.
- 2 is invertible in R.

**Proof outline.**

1. Expand B(x+y,x+y)=B(x,x)+B(x,y)+B(y,x)+B(y,y) by bilinearity.
2. Collect terms and cancel the transpose terms; use ½·2=1. This is exactly the rescaling identity for α=½(B−Bᵀ), β=B and cochain q.

**Acceptance.**

- For B(x,y)=x₀y₁ and x=e₀,y=e₁ over Q, the left side is ½+½=1.
- The plus sign before q(x+y) is required for the forward coordinate map t↦t+q(x).
- The identity holds for degenerate and symmetric forms.

<a id="mp0-polarization-equivalence"></a>
#### Polarized Heisenberg coordinates

`MP.0/polarization-equivalence` · construction · part MP.0

For scalar B and invertible 2, construct E_{½(B−Bᵀ)}≃E_B by (t,x)↦(t+½B(x,x),x), with inverse (t,x)↦(t−½B(x,x),x). This is a specialization of the native equivalence of rescaled extensions.

**Hypotheses.**

- R is a commutative ring and W,W′,W″ are R-modules with additive commutative groups. Forms are native scalar-valued bilinear forms, with no nondegeneracy assumption unless explicitly stated.
- E_B denotes the same native extension, with coordinates (t,w). Maps between extensions fix the coefficient coordinate.
- 2 is invertible in R.

**Construction.**

1. Use polarization-cocycle as the cochain identity required by native FactorSet.rescaleEquiv, under the trivial action.
2. Extract its underlying group isomorphism. Native forward and inverse rescaling formulas give the two coordinate descriptions; q(0)=0 shows compatibility with the central inclusion.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.Metaplectic.Heisenberg.polarizationEquiv_apply` (projection): The forward coefficient is t+½B(x,x), and the quotient coordinate remains x.
- `TauCeti.Metaplectic.Heisenberg.polarizationEquiv_symm_apply` (projection): The inverse coefficient is t−½B(x,x), and the quotient coordinate remains x.
- `TauCeti.Metaplectic.Heisenberg.polarizationEquiv_inl` (compatibility): The equivalence fixes the native coefficient injection.

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.Metaplectic.Heisenberg.polarizationEquiv_zero` (degenerate): For B=0 on Q, the equivalence fixes (3,4).
- `TauCeti.Metaplectic.Heisenberg.polarizationEquiv_cross` (computation): For B(x,y)=x₀y₁ on Q², the image of (0,(2,3)) is (3,(2,3)).
- `TauCeti.Metaplectic.Heisenberg.polarizationEquiv_sign` (non-example): For the same B, the inverse image of (0,(2,3)) is (−3,(2,3)); using a plus sign for both directions fails.

**Acceptance.**

- For the standard polarization W=X⊕Y with B((x,y),(x′,y′))=ω(x,y′), the correction is ½ω(x,y).
- This construction assumes a chosen polarized bilinear representative; existence of a Lagrangian complement belongs to the existing LV.3 node.

<a id="mp0-central-character-criterion"></a>
#### Criterion for the section-trivial central character

`MP.0/central-character-criterion` · theorem · part MP.0

For any group A and homomorphism χ:Multiplicative C→A, the function E_B→A given by (t,x)↦χ(t) preserves multiplication iff χ(B(x,y))=1 for every x,y∈W.

**Hypotheses.**

- R is a commutative ring; W and C are additive commutative groups and R-modules. B:W×W→C is a native R-bilinear map.
- Write E_B for the existing FactorSet.Extension of the bilinear factor set. This is notation, not a proposed wrapper. Coordinates are (t,w), coefficient first; identity is (0,0). The coefficient action is the native trivial action.
- A is any group; χ is a group homomorphism from Multiplicative C to A.

**Proof outline.**

1. Necessity: test multiplicativity on (0,x) and (0,y). Both proposed character values are one, and the product has coefficient B(x,y).
2. Sufficiency: apply χ to t+s+B(x,y), use its homomorphism law, and use χ(B(x,y))=1. Its value at the identity is already one. No commutativity of A is required.

**Acceptance.**

- For B=0 every χ satisfies the criterion.
- For B(x,y)=x₀y₁ over Z and χ the identity on Multiplicative Z, the proposed scalar projection is not multiplicative.
- For B=½ω restricted to a lattice, killing ω on the lattice is insufficient unless χ also kills ½ω; the Q₂ counterexample is recorded in E-MP0-3.

**Depends on.** this roadmap: [`MP.0/bilinear-factor-set`](#mp0-bilinear-factor-set); libraries: `tauceti:TauCeti.FactorSet.Extension.mul_left`.

**Used in this roadmap by.** [`MP.0/central-character`](#mp0-central-character).

- `Kudla96`, I.2, p.6, the asserted extension ψ_Y; corrected statement; excerpt at PDF6: “unique extension ψY to H(Y ) , given by ψY (y, t) = ψ(t) . Let” — The source formula requires exactly the cocycle-killing condition proved here. For an isotropic F-subspace it holds because the form itself vanishes; character-self-duality of an arbitrary additive subgroup alone does not suffice.

<a id="mp0-central-character"></a>
#### Section-trivial extension of a central character

`MP.0/central-character` · construction · planet “Heisenberg central character” · part MP.0

Given χ:Multiplicative C→A with χ(B(x,y))=1 for all x,y, construct the group homomorphism E_B→A, (t,x)↦χ(t). It extends χ on native inl and is trivial on the native canonical section.

**Hypotheses.**

- R is a commutative ring; W and C are additive commutative groups and R-modules. B:W×W→C is a native R-bilinear map.
- Write E_B for the existing FactorSet.Extension of the bilinear factor set. This is notation, not a proposed wrapper. Coordinates are (t,w), coefficient first; identity is (0,0). The coefficient action is the native trivial action.
- A is any group; χ:Multiplicative C→A is a group homomorphism, and χ(B(x,y))=1 for every x,y.

**Construction.**

1. Use central-character-criterion to establish multiplicativity and the homomorphism law for χ to establish the identity value.
2. Use the coordinate formula to check the two prescribed restrictions. For uniqueness among homomorphisms satisfying both restrictions, factor each p as inl(p.left) times canonicalSection(p.right) using the native decomposition theorem.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.Metaplectic.Heisenberg.centralCharacter_apply` (projection): At (t,x) the homomorphism evaluates to χ(t).
- `TauCeti.Metaplectic.Heisenberg.centralCharacter_inl` (compatibility): Its restriction along native inl is χ.
- `TauCeti.Metaplectic.Heisenberg.centralCharacter_canonicalSection` (simp): Its value on each native canonicalSection(x) is one.
- `TauCeti.Metaplectic.Heisenberg.centralCharacter_unique` (universal-property): If ρ:E_B→A agrees with χ on native inl and is one on every native canonicalSection(x), then ρ equals centralCharacter B χ. Both conditions are required.

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.Metaplectic.Heisenberg.centralCharacter_value` (computation): For B=0 on Z and χ the identity of Multiplicative Z, the value at (3,4) is additive 3.
- `TauCeti.Metaplectic.Heisenberg.centralCharacter_trivial` (degenerate): For every bilinear B, the trivial character into Multiplicative Z gives the trivial homomorphism on E_B.
- `TauCeti.Metaplectic.Heisenberg.centralCharacter_zero` (compatibility): For B=0 on Z and χ the native identity homomorphism, the value at the native extension identity is one.

**Acceptance.**

- Uniqueness is asserted only with both the central restriction and triviality on the chosen section.
- The section need not itself be a homomorphism; the cocycle condition makes its image trivial under this character.
- An arbitrary extension of the same χ may be multiplied by a nontrivial character of the quotient.

**Uses.**

- Kudla I.2, pp.6–7; MP.0: Supply the inducing character of H(Y) when Y is an isotropic subspace, or when an explicit splitting condition has been established.
- Kudla I.1 Theorem 1.1, p.3; MP.1: Specify the central character of the chosen model. This construction does not prove irreducibility or Stone–von Neumann uniqueness.

**Depends on.** this roadmap: [`MP.0/bilinear-factor-set`](#mp0-bilinear-factor-set), [`MP.0/central-character-criterion`](#mp0-central-character-criterion); libraries: `tauceti:TauCeti.FactorSet.inl`, `tauceti:TauCeti.FactorSet.canonicalSection`, `tauceti:TauCeti.FactorSet.inl_mul_canonicalSection`.

**Library.** module `TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Metaplectic/Heisenberg`, namespace `TauCeti.Metaplectic.Heisenberg`, declaration `TauCeti.Metaplectic.Heisenberg.centralCharacter`.

**Sources.**

- `Kudla96`, I.2, p.6, extension ψ_Y; corrected normalization and hypothesis; excerpt at PDF6: “unique extension ψY to H(Y ) , given by ψY (y, t) = ψ(t) . Let” — This is the distinguished character intended in the induced model, with the missing cocycle hypothesis and the normalization needed for uniqueness made explicit.

### MP.0:schroedinger — Topology, Haar measure and Schrödinger models

<a id="mp0-topological-heisenberg"></a>
#### Topological Heisenberg extension

`MP.0/topological-heisenberg` · construction · part MP.0

Give the existing bilinear FactorSet.Extension E_B the topology transported from C×W by its coordinate equivalence. If C,W are Hausdorff topological modules and B is continuous, multiplication and inversion are continuous. For finite-dimensional modules over a nondiscrete local field it is locally compact and second countable. For B=½ω, the native isometry action is jointly continuous.

**Hypotheses.**

- The local-field specialization has characteristic different from two; W is finite dimensional and ω is alternating. Continuity of B is required in the general topological-module case.

**Construction.**

1. Use the inherited coordinate multiplication and inverse formulas; sums, B and negation are continuous.
2. Transport the product topology and local compactness, then identify isometries with the closed subgroup of the finite-dimensional general linear group preserving ω.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.Metaplectic.heisenbergCoordinates` (equivalence): The native extension coordinate equivalence E_B≃C×W is a homeomorphism.
- `TauCeti.Metaplectic.heisenberg_continuous_mul` (structure): Multiplication is continuous for the transported product topology.
- `TauCeti.Metaplectic.heisenberg_continuous_action` (compatibility): The native form-isometry group acts jointly continuously on E_{½ω}.

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.Metaplectic.heisenbergTopology_zero` (degenerate): For W=0 over R the coordinate homeomorphism identifies E with the additive topological group R.
- `TauCeti.Metaplectic.heisenbergTopology_q2` (compatibility): For W=Q₂² with standard ω, the topology is precisely Q₂×Q₂² and the half-form multiplication is continuous.
- `TauCeti.Metaplectic.heisenbergTopology_projection` (characterisation): The central inclusion is a closed embedding and the quotient projection is an open continuous surjection.

**Acceptance.**

- Q₂ is admitted: the field element 2 is invertible although it is not an integral unit.

**Uses.**

- Weil III.§§31–36; MP.1: Form a topological, rather than merely abstract, normalizer extension.

**Prototype boundary.** The Q₂ product-topology test is generalized to native topological field/module parameters; local compactness and action-group topology require the packet hypotheses. The generic action API takes joint continuity of native isometry evaluation; an arbitrary topology on that group does not suffice.

**Depends on.** this roadmap: [`MP.0/bilinear-factor-set`](#mp0-bilinear-factor-set), [`MP.0/inverse`](#mp0-inverse), [`MP.0/isometry-action`](#mp0-isometry-action).

<a id="mp0-heisenberg-haar"></a>
#### Product Haar measure on the Heisenberg group

`MP.0/heisenberg-haar` · theorem · part MP.0

For C=F, W=F^{2n}, B continuous bilinear, the product of additive Haar measures μ_F and μ_W transported to E_B is both left and right Haar measure. With self-dual measures for ψ and ω, every symplectic automorphism preserves it; rescaling the central or vector measure rescales their product.

**Hypotheses.**

- F is a nondiscrete local field; for symplectic invariance ω is nondegenerate.

**Proof outline.**

1. Fix one coordinate in the left-translation formula and apply translation invariance in the coefficient coordinate, then in W; use Fubini. Repeat on the right.
2. In the symplectic case determinant one gives vector-measure invariance. Import finite-dimensional self-dual Haar and change of variables from the Fourier supplier.

**Acceptance.**

- For n=0 the measure is μ_F. No arbitrary probability normalization is imposed on a noncompact field.

**Prototype boundary.** The standard native-fragment boundary (see Conventions).

**Open inputs (gaps).**

- [G0.1](#g0-1) *Product Haar measure on the Heisenberg group proof/signature boundary.* AL.0 currently states Fourier inversion on the scalar local field. Its finite-dimensional vector-space extension, measure determinant law, and the symplectic determinant-one bridge must be supplied and checked before this signature is closed.

**Requests.** [R0.1](#r0-1) to `AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors:AL.0`.

**Depends on.** this roadmap: [`MP.0/topological-heisenberg`](#mp0-topological-heisenberg); other roadmaps: `AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors:AL.0/local-fourier-inversion`, `AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors:AL.0`.

<a id="mp0-schroedinger-model"></a>
#### Schrödinger representation

`MP.0/schroedinger-model` · construction · planet “Schrödinger representation” · part MP.0

For W=X⊕Y with X,Y Lagrangian, define on S(X) the representation ρψ(x+y,t)φ(u)=ψ(t+ω(u,y)+½ω(x,y))φ(u+x). Here S(X) is the actual locally constant compactly supported space at nonarchimedean places and the joint real Schwartz space at archimedean places. The formula preserves S(X) and gives central character ψ.

**Hypotheses.**

- F is a nondiscrete local field of characteristic different from two; ψ is nontrivial continuous unitary; the polarization identifies Y with the algebraic dual of X by ω.

**Construction.**

1. Import the Lagrangian complement and basis theorem from LV.3 and the concrete finite-dimensional Schwartz carrier from AL.0.
2. Compose the two displayed operators; the cross term is exactly ½ω(w,w′), hence the inherited group law. Translation and multiplication by a character preserve the appropriate Schwartz space.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.Metaplectic.schroedinger_apply` (simp): Evaluation is the displayed translation and modulation formula.
- `TauCeti.Metaplectic.schroedinger_center` (simp): ρψ(0,t)φ=ψ(t)φ.
- `TauCeti.Metaplectic.schroedinger_mul` (relation): ρψ(hh′)=ρψ(h)ρψ(h′).
- `TauCeti.Metaplectic.schroedinger_isUnitary` (compatibility): The induced operator on L²(X,μselfdual) is a native linear isometry and its map to continuous linear operators is unitary.

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.Metaplectic.schroedinger_zero` (degenerate): When X=Y=0, ρψ(t) is multiplication by ψ(t) on C.
- `TauCeti.Metaplectic.schroedinger_translation` (computation): For w=x∈X, ρψ(x,0)φ(u)=φ(u+x).
- `TauCeti.Metaplectic.schroedinger_modulation` (computation): For w=y∈Y, ρψ(y,0)φ(u)=ψ(ω(u,y))φ(u).
- `TauCeti.Metaplectic.schroedinger_commutator` (non-example): For x∈X,y∈Y, ρ(x)ρ(y)=ψ(ω(x,y))ρ(y)ρ(x), with this positive sign.

**Acceptance.**

- The center acts by ψ, and modulation and translation have the required ordered commutator.

**Uses.**

- Kudla I.2 Prop.2.3; MP.1–2: Supply the concrete oscillator carrier for intertwiners and generators.

**Prototype boundary.** Function-space action fragment. The requested local Schwartz carrier, Schwartz preservation and actual L² descent are not replaced by arbitrary structure fields; the unitarity signature takes the resulting native Hilbert action.

**Open inputs (gaps).**

- [G0.2](#g0-2) *Schrödinger representation proof/signature boundary.* The exact finite-dimensional and joint archimedean Schwartz carriers are an AL.0 Part II request; neither a formal function symbol nor the scalar supplier alone supplies them.

<a id="mp0-induced-schroedinger"></a>
#### Induced and coordinate Schrödinger models

`MP.0/induced-schroedinger` · construction · part MP.0

Identify S(X) with the smooth functions f on H(W) satisfying f(h_Yh)=ψ_Y(h_Y)f(h), whose support is compact modulo H(Y), by evaluation on the X section; here H(Y)=Y×F and ψ_Y(y,t)=ψ(t). The inverse is the extension determined by covariance. Right translation gives exactly the Schrödinger formula.

**Hypotheses.**

- F is nonarchimedean; ψ is continuous nontrivial unitary; Y is an isotropic F-subspace, not merely a character-self-dual lattice.

**Construction.**

1. Use unique H(Y) times X decomposition, calculate its central coordinate and impose covariance.
2. Support modulo H(Y) is precisely compact support on X. Import smooth induction from SR.2; check sign using Kudla’s right-translation convention.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.Metaplectic.inducedSchroedingerEquiv_apply` (simp): The coordinate map is f↦(u↦f(u,0)).
- `TauCeti.Metaplectic.inducedSchroedingerEquiv_covariance` (characterisation): The inverse has ψ_Y covariance and compact support modulo H(Y).
- `TauCeti.Metaplectic.inducedSchroedingerEquiv_intertwines` (compatibility): The equivalence intertwines right translation with ρψ.

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.Metaplectic.inducedSchroedingerEquiv_zero` (degenerate): For W=0 the induced model is the one-dimensional central character.
- `TauCeti.Metaplectic.inducedSchroedingerEquiv_indicator` (computation): A compact open L⊂X gives a vector whose section restriction is exactly 1_L.
- `TauCeti.Metaplectic.inducedSchroedingerEquiv_dyadic` (non-example): The subgroup Z₂²⊂Q₂² with standard ω does not admit ψ_Y(y,t)=ψ(t) when ψ has conductor Z₂, because ψ(½ω(e₀,e₁))=−1.

**Acceptance.**

- This is an equivalence of actual smooth representations, not the algebraic polarization cochain map.

**Uses.**

- Kudla I.2 Prop.2.3; MP.1: Derive quotient-integral intertwiners from the induced realization.

**Prototype boundary.** Section-evaluation/covariance fragment. The subtype states an explicit equation, not a placeholder Prop field. Smooth compact induction and its support condition await SR.2; the dyadic obstruction is expressed on its rational half argument.

**Requests.** [R0.2](#r0-2) to `SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups:SR.2`.

**Independent review** (REV-MetaplecticAutomorphicForms--MP.0): *unverifiable.* Checked source Kudla96, I.2 Lemma2.2, PDF7, polarization realization; literal excerpt PDF7. Section evaluation/covariance are valid function-space fragments and the dyadic obstruction is retained. The intertwining API permits unrelated translation and rho: take translation identically zero and rho trivial to get0=f. It does not state the actual compact-induction equivalence.

<a id="mp0-hilbert-schroedinger"></a>
#### Hilbert Schrödinger model

`MP.0/hilbert-schroedinger` · construction · part MP.0

Extend translation and modulation to unitary operators on the actual Hilbert space L²(X,μselfdual), using almost-everywhere classes. This is a strongly continuous unitary representation of H(W); its dense Schwartz subspace carries the preceding formula.

**Hypotheses.**

- F is a local field of characteristic different from two; X is finite dimensional; ψ is continuous unitary.

**Construction.**

1. Translations preserve Haar measure and modulation has absolute value one, so the operators descend to L² and preserve its inner product.
2. Prove strong continuity first on Schwartz vectors by dominated convergence and then by density. Native ContRepresentation requires an additional strong-continuity assertion in the group variable.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.Metaplectic.hilbertSchroedinger_norm` (simp): Every ρψ(h) preserves the L² norm.
- `TauCeti.Metaplectic.hilbertSchroedinger_schwartz` (compatibility): The Schwartz-to-L² dense inclusion intertwines the two actions.
- `TauCeti.Metaplectic.hilbertSchroedinger_stronglyContinuous` (structure): For every ξ∈L², h↦ρψ(h)ξ is continuous.

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.Metaplectic.hilbertSchroedinger_zero` (degenerate): For X=0 the Hilbert space is C and the representation is ψ.
- `TauCeti.Metaplectic.hilbertSchroedinger_gaussian` (computation): On X=R, translation of e^{−πu²} gives e^{−π(u+x)²} with identical L² norm.
- `TauCeti.Metaplectic.hilbertSchroedinger_ae` (compatibility): Changing a measurable representative on a null set does not change any represented L² vector.

**Acceptance.**

- Continuity is not inferred from native ContRepresentation’s name.

**Uses.**

- Weil I.§10; MP.1: Define the normalizer in the unitary group with the strong operator topology.

**Prototype boundary.** H denotes the actual L² space after supplier instantiation; this fragment does not manufacture a Hilbert space or assert every ContRepresentation is strongly continuous. L² null representatives are equal vectors.

**Open inputs (gaps).**

- [G0.3](#g0-3) *Hilbert Schrödinger model proof/signature boundary.* Native L² density and finite-dimensional local-field measure input must be instantiated; an abstract norm-preserving monoid homomorphism alone is not the required strongly continuous model.

<a id="mp0-smooth-vectors"></a>
#### Smooth vectors of the oscillator model

`MP.0/smooth-vectors` · comparison · part MP.0

At nonarchimedean places the smooth vectors of the Hilbert oscillator model are precisely S(X). Over R, and over C viewed as a real field, the C∞ vectors for the Heisenberg group action are precisely the Schwartz functions on the underlying real X, with their Schwartz Fréchet topology.

**Hypotheses.**

- The local unitary model has nontrivial central character. Archimedean smoothness means all orbit derivatives for the full Heisenberg group, not just smooth pointwise representatives.

**Proof outline.**

1. Nonarchimedean compact-open stabilizers force local constancy and compact support using translations and modulations.
2. In the real model the infinitesimal operators are partial derivatives and coordinate multiplications. Joint Sobolev estimates identify their common domain with Schwartz space.

**Acceptance.**

- Smooth vectors include modulation derivatives; arbitrary smooth L² functions need not be Schwartz.

**Prototype boundary.** Real one-dimensional Schrödinger specialization, using all three Heisenberg coordinates (t,x,y). H is the actual L² space, i its Schwartz injection and orbit its strongly continuous Schrödinger action; those supplier identifications are omitted. Smoothness of a single translation or central orbit is insufficient.

**Open inputs (gaps).**

- [G0.4](#g0-4) *Smooth vectors of the oscillator model proof/signature boundary.* The nonarchimedean compact-open argument and the archimedean Sobolev/Fréchet comparison require a matching proof source and a native smooth-vector carrier from SR.0/AF.1. The source citation here does not establish the archimedean conclusion.

**Requests.** [R0.3](#r0-3) to `AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups:AF.1`; [R0.4](#r0-4) to `SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups:SR.0:abelian-category`.

**Depends on.** this roadmap: [`MP.0/hilbert-schroedinger`](#mp0-hilbert-schroedinger), [`MP.0/schroedinger-model`](#mp0-schroedinger-model); other roadmaps: `AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups:AF.1`, `SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups:SR.0:abelian-category`; libraries: `mathlib:SchwartzMap`, `mathlib:ContRepresentation`.
